description: Experiment D-scale (Phase 15 ruling 2, work order 3, cloud window 3). The same request mix as exp-d-query-load-v1 (closed-loop GET on graph-evidence-api through the ALB: /v1/evidence/<id>, /v1/graph/nodes/<researcherId>, /v1/graph/nodes/<researcherId>/neighbors with direction both, depth 1, limit 50, COAUTHORED_WITH; IDs from the latest PASS smoke record), held at one level, concurrency 8, for 600 s, then 1,500 s of post-observation with no load. No /v1/query, so no Haiku or Bedrock call. Purpose: observe one target-tracking scale-out and one scale-in of graph-evidence-api (1 to 2 tasks). EXPERIMENT SETTING, NOT A TUNED PRODUCTION VALUE: the target-tracking CPU target is 15 percent (Terraform variable service_cpu_target_percent = 15 in course.tfvars for window 3; the variable default and production value is 60). Reason (ruling 2): in window 2, graph-evidence-api averaged 20 to 27 percent CPU at concurrency 8 (about 2,150 requests per minute) while Neptune db.t4g.medium reached 80 to 93 percent CPU, so a 60 percent target was never reached and nothing scaled. Every 30 s during the load and the post-observation, the harness samples desired, running and pending task counts (read-only describe-services) into raw/ecs-timeline.csv. After the post-observation it collects, read-only and in UTC, the Application Auto Scaling scaling activities and policies, the ECS service events, the target-tracking alarms and their history, and CloudWatch 1-minute metrics (see metrics). A failed collection is recorded in raw/collect.json and its collect-<name>.json and does not change the exit code or summary.json. Run by the human through scripts/run-experiment.sh after deploy.sh --resume, the Neptune warm-up and a PASS smoke-test.sh in window 3.

limits.maxMinutesReason: Phase 15 ruling 6 (code review 1 m3): at least 5 minutes above the harness's own waits (Phase 14 ruling 34). Worst case with every wait at its bound: setup about 3 s (window 2) + preflight 60 s (6 GETs, 10 s timeout) + 3 ecs describe-services reads 60 s (20 s subprocess timeout each) + 600 s load + 30 s worker tail + 1,500 s post-observation + 20 s poller join + 90 s collection = 2,363 s, about 39.4 min, 5.6 min under 45
limits.plannedBreakdown: setup (terraform output, sts, secret) under 1 min; preflight seconds; 600 s load; 1,500 s post-observation; collection at most 90 s
limits.maxRequestsPerLevelReason: window 2 ran about 36 requests per second at concurrency 8, so 600 s is about 21,500 requests, above the 20,000 default cap
limits.abortScope: unchanged from exp-d-query-load-v1: per request kind, a sliding window within the level and the whole level; preflight GET of each path first
limits.exitCodes: 0 the level ran; 1 abort rule; 2 usage; 3 precondition or non-2xx preflight; 4 unexpected error. Collection never changes the exit code.
limits.awsCallsByHarness: read-only only: sts get-caller-identity, secretsmanager get-secret-value (API key, memory only), ecs describe-services, application-autoscaling describe-scaling-activities and describe-scaling-policies, cloudwatch describe-alarms, describe-alarm-history and get-metric-data; the collection calls are allowlisted in the harness (READ_ONLY_CALLS)
limits.cpuTargetIs: an experiment setting for window 3 (Phase 15 ruling 2), not a tuned production value; production default 60
limits.scaleChanges: none by the harness; Application Auto Scaling may move graph-evidence-api between 1 and 2 tasks (Terraform service_max_counts.graph_evidence_api = 2, cpu target 15, scale-out cooldown 60 s, scale-in cooldown 120 s)
limits.budgetNote: incremental cost of the run only (one extra Fargate task for at most about 25 minutes, ALB requests, Neptune I/O, about 9 CloudWatch metric series in one get-metric-data call); the window's runtime hours are counted in the window 3 budget (ruling 3)

expectedFinding: Stated before the run and reported either way (ruling 2): with the CPU target at 15 percent, one sustained concurrency-8 level should trigger one scale-out (the high alarm needs 3 minutes above target) and, after the load stops, one scale-in (the low alarm needs about 15 minutes below its threshold; both alarms' exact thresholds and periods are recorded in raw/collect-alarms.json). A second task is expected to add no throughput while Neptune (db.t4g.medium) is the bottleneck: requests per second and latency after the second task is healthy should match the single-task period within noise, and Neptune CPU should stay high. If no scale-out, no scale-in, or a throughput gain is observed, that is the reported result.

context.neptuneInstanceClassDuringRun: db.t4g.medium (the bulk load runs on db.r6g.large, then the instance returns to db.t4g.medium before the run; Phase 14 rulings 42 and 43)
context.servicesImage: the image deploy.sh --resume deploys at the window 3 HEAD; its package record under operations/releases/ is the authority, not known when this manifest is written
context.runtimeStores: loaded by load-stores.sh in window 3 from the window 2 S3 objects (ruling 3); the run IDs are those in the window 3 load-stores record, expected to match exp-d-query-load-v1's context
context.comparisonRun: experiments/results/exp-d-query-load-v1/20261118T063904Z (window 2; concurrency 8 level: 6,439 requests in 180 s, about 35.7 per second, 0 errors, desired stayed 1)
context.inputs: terraform output (alb_dns_name, api_key_secret_arn, ecs_cluster_name, account_id, runtime_enabled, alb_arn_suffix, neptune_cluster_id); Secrets Manager API key (memory only); latest PASS operations/releases/smoke-*.json
context.rawOutputs: inputs.json, preflight.json, requests-c8.csv, ecs-before-c8.json, ecs-after-c8.json, ecs-post-observe.json, summary.json (written before the collection), ecs-timeline.csv (utc, desired, running, pending, error every 30 s), collect.json (index: metrics interval, target group ARN, skipped metric queries, each call's time and error), collect-scaling-activities.json, collect-scaling-policies.json, collect-ecs-service.json (events and loadBalancers), collect-alarms.json, collect-alarm-history-<n>.json, collect-metrics.json (get-metric-data output and its queries)
context.metricsInterval: from 5 minutes before the harness start (minute-aligned, UTC) to the minute after collection; period 60 s
context.metricsNote: TargetGroup is the suffix of the targetGroupArn in describe-services loadBalancers, found at collection time; LoadBalancer is terraform output alb_arn_suffix; DBClusterIdentifier is terraform output neptune_cluster_id. All three are recorded in raw/collect-metrics.json. Container Insights is disabled, so task counts come from describe-services, not CloudWatch.
